finding: emitServerSocketEOFNT(self, req) sets req[eofInProgress] but schedules process.nextTick(emitServerSocketEOF, self) without forwarding req. The callback only pushes EOF to the IncomingMessage and sets complete when it receives req.

dependentSource.condition: IncomingMessage._read returns early when eofInProgress is true.

conditionalConsequence: If the socket-resume completed-buffer branch invokes this helper with an actual req, the request may receive its buffered data while the queued callback only ends the socket-readable side; its own EOF/complete may remain absent and later _read calls can return early.
unproven: Whether the real installed requests execute this branch.
Whether another platform callback emits the missing request EOF.
Whether this is the actual cause of run04 or run05 behavior.
Whether native Readable.toWeb changes ordering sufficiently to avoid that branch.

analysis: The abstract read→latch.close pattern can lose a synchronously emitted readable event if read returns null and no further terminal/data event follows.

Bun's normal Readable.read marks kSync around _read, defers corresponding readable notification to nextTick, recalculates the returned amount when _read pushes synchronously and schedules terminal end on nextTick.
Effect onEnd/onError also store exit.current before opening; loop checks it before waiting. Latch.await checks isOpen when registering.

No I/O event interleaves between synchronous read returning and latch.close in the same JavaScript stack. A custom read override or nonstandard synchronous event could differ, but none is established here.

nativeAdapterDifference.behavior: Native Readable.toWeb uses flowing data/pause/resume and finished, whereas the Effect NodeStream adapter pulls with readable.read/latch. Different event ordering is a testable hypothesis, not a verified correction.

nextProof: Use run05 and, only after protected-owner authorization, a tightly bounded phase trace or candidate comparison that records first byte/EOF/handler completion without bodies or identity data.
